subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime session mutations uniformly fail closed on legacy ownerless rows, and should this PR own the shared create/reset/delete helper while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103534 reuses it for patch?
rationale: Exact owner equality closes a transcript and metadata isolation gap, but ownerless legacy rows have no attributable plugin owner; choosing rejection versus migration or temporary compatibility changes existing upgrade behavior and must be consistent across all mutation methods.

options.title: Approve fail-closed and consolidate
options.body: Use one shared helper across create, reset, delete, and patch, reject ownerless rows for plugin runtimes, and require live Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Add an explicit migration path
options.body: Define a doctor or operator-owned migration that assigns or resolves legacy ownership before enforcing exact equality at runtime.

options.title: Preserve temporary legacy access
options.body: Allow plugin runtimes to use ownerless rows during a documented deprecation window with a concrete removal plan.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed and consolidate
recommendation.body: Use one shared helper across create, reset, delete, and patch, reject ownerless rows for plugin runtimes, and require live Gateway proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review and contributor discussion already route the legacy ownerless-session security and compatibility decision to Takhoffman.
